guitar.modelsText: Fender Stratocaster (Two-Tone Sunburst signature) / PRS Silver Sky
guitar.notes: Confirmed — John Mayer has had a long-documented signature relationship with Fender Stratocasters and more recently PRS Silver Sky.

tone.target: clean Fender-style edge-of-breakup with slight compression
tone.profile: clean Fender-style edge-of-breakup with slight compression
tone.summary: A pristine signal chain utilizing compression for dynamics, followed by a mild boost to enhance the arpeggios, feeding into a US Deluxe/Silver Twin style amp setup paired with a 2x12 cabinet for classic clean headroom and Fender character. Room reverb adds necessary space without muddying the clarity.
corrections: drop chorus; keep it mostly dry
favor clean-to-grit breakup over blues-rock drive

rig.name: John Mayer - Why Georgia - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.

Provide a subtle lift and enhance the arpeggiated notes.

blocks.gap: The Red Haze is typically used for fuzz/psychedelic tones, but its low drive setting can simulate the gentle breakup of a Fender amp when pushed lightly.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the clean headroom and classic Fender character.

Enhance the clear top end and articulate the arpeggios.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism and overall clarity by swapping the default IR for a more open-sounding Fender 2x12.

proposals.reason: Enhance classic clean headroom and clarity, matching the desired Fender tone.
